title: OTTER: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Text-Aware Visual Feature Extraction
creator: Huang Huang, Fangchen Liu, Letian Fu, Tingfan Wu, Mustafa Mukadam, Jitendra Malik, Ken Goldberg, Pieter Abbeel
description: Abstract Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models aim to predict robotic actions based on visual observations and language instructions. Existing approaches require fine-tuning pre-trained vision-language models (VLMs) as visual and language features are independently fed into downstream policies, degrading the pre-trained semantic alignments. We propose OTTER, a novel VLA architecture that leverages these existing alignments through explicit, text-aware visual feature extraction.

title: Peaky Finders: Characterizing Double-peaked Type IIb Supernovae in Large-Scale Live-Stream Photometric Surveys Facilities: ATLAS, ZTF ANTARES ( Matheson et al. 2021 ) , corner ( Foreman-Mackey et al. 2016 ) , dustmaps ( Green 2018 ) , emcee ( Foreman-Mackey et al. 2013 ) , extinction ( Barbary 2021
creator: Adrian Crawford, Tyler A. Pritchard, Maryam Modjaz, Craig Pellegrino, Sahana Kumar, Raphael Baer-Way
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Adrian Crawford, Tyler A. Pritchard, Maryam Modjaz, Craig Pellegrino, Sahana Kumar, Raphael Baer-Way. We present the first photometric population study of double-peaked Type IIb supernovae (SNe IIb). SNe IIb are produced from the core-collapse of massive stars whose outermost Hydrogen layer has been partially stripped prior to explosion. These double-peaked light curves, consisting of a shock-cooling emission peak (SCE) followed by the main nickel-powered peak, contain more crucial information about the progenitor system than the typical single-peaked light curves.

title: Understanding entropy production via a thermal zero-player game
creator: M. Süzen
description: Abstract A new thermal bath scheme for Ising-Conway Entropy Game (ICEg) is introduced. New game moves in sampling the given temperature is achieved via Monte Carlo dynamics of both Metropolis and Glauber as a stochastic game. This kind of approach makes the game an ideal tool for demonstrating thermal dependency of entropy production in a novel way.

title: Curating Demonstrations using Online Experience
creator: Annie S. Chen, Alec M. Lessing, Yuejiang Liu, Chelsea FinnStanford University
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Annie S. Chen, Alec M. Lessing, Yuejiang Liu, Chelsea FinnStanford University. Many robot demonstration datasets contain heterogeneous demonstrations of varying quality. This heterogeneity may benefit policy pre-training, but can hinder robot performance when used with a final imitation learning objective. In particular, some strategies in the data may be less reliable than others or may be underrepresented in the data, leading to poor performance when such strategies are sampled at test time.

title: Observables and Unconstrained Spin Tensor Dynamics in General Relativity from Scattering Amplitudes
creator: Mark Alaverdian, Zvi Bern, Dimitrios Kosmopoulos, Andres Luna, Radu Roiban, Trevor Scheopner, Fei Teng
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Mark Alaverdian, Zvi Bern, Dimitrios Kosmopoulos, Andres Luna, Radu Roiban, Trevor Scheopner, Fei Teng. In a previous Letter, we showed that physical scattering observables for compact spinning objects in general relativity can depend on additional degrees of freedom in the spin tensor beyond those described by the spin vector alone.

title: Generating Novel Brain Morphology by Deforming Learned Templates
creator: Alan Q. Wang, Fangrui Huang, Bailey Trang, Wei Peng, Mohammad Abbasi, Kilian Pohl, Mert Sabuncu, Ehsan Adeli
description: Abstract Designing generative models for 3D structural brain MRI that synthesize morphologically-plausible and attribute-specific (e.g., age, sex, disease state) samples is an active area of research. Existing approaches based on frameworks like GANs or diffusion models synthesize the image directly, which may limit their ability to capture intricate morphological details.

title: Accelerating Focal Search in Multi-Agent Path Finding with Tighter Lower Bounds
creator: Yimin Tang, Zhenghong Yu, Jiaoyang Li, Sven Koenig
description: Abstract Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) involves finding collision-free paths for multiple agents while minimizing a cost function—an NP-hard problem. Bounded suboptimal methods like Enhanced Conflict-Based Search (ECBS) and Explicit Estimation CBS (EECBS) balance solution quality with computational efficiency using focal search mechanisms.

title: Tackling Few-Shot Segmentation in Remote Sensing via Inpainting Diffusion Model
creator: Steve Andreas Immanuel, Woojin Cho, Junhyuk Heo, Darongsae Kwon
description: Abstract Limited data is a common problem in remote sensing due to the high cost of obtaining annotated samples. In the few-shot segmentation task, models are typically trained on base classes with abundant annotations and later adapted to novel classes with limited examples. However, this often necessitates specialized model architectures or complex training strategies.

title: Predicting Team Performance from Communications in Simulated Search-and-Rescue Conference: Proc. of the 24th International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems (AAMAS 2025); May 19 – 23, 2025; Detroit, Michigan, USA ea0109
creator: Ali Jalal-Kamali, Nikolos M. Gurney, David V. Pynadath
description: Abstract . Understanding how individual traits influence team performance is valuable, but these traits are not always directly observable. Prior research has inferred traits like trust from behavioral data. We analyze conversational data to identify team traits and their correlation with teaming outcomes.

title: DeepGrav: Anomalous Gravitational-Wave Detection Through Deep Latent Features
creator: Jianqi Yan, Alex P. LeungDepartment of PhysicsThe University of Hong KongHong Kong {easonyan, alexpl}@hku.hk, Zhiyuan Pei Faculty of Innovation EngineeringMacau University of Science and TechnologyMacau 2109853eii30002@student.must.edu.mo, David C.
